explanation: It comes from Greek palin, again, and dromos, running. Whole sentences can do it too, if you ignore spaces and punctuation: 'Was it a car or a cat I saw?'

claims.text: A palindrome is a word or phrase that reads the same backwards as forwards.
An anagram rearranges letters, a homonym shares spelling or sound with another word, and an acronym is formed from initial letters.
Palindrome comes from Greek palin (again) and dromos (running).
'Was it a car or a cat I saw?' reads the same backwards when spaces and punctuation are ignored.
